heading: If you’re a parent or starting a family
intro: The rate a country reports shapes where midwives, equipment and money go. When newborn deaths are undercounted, the places that need help most can look like they’re doing fine.

heading: If you work in a hospital
intro: Reporting every month, and writing down a real zero instead of leaving a blank, is what turns your ward’s reality into the national picture. Gaps here erase your sickest babies from the record.

heading: If you shape health policy
intro: Decisions rest on these numbers. If the routine system captures only a fraction of deaths, targets can look met while the problem persists.

heading: If you’re a student or researcher
intro: This is a case study in data quality: completeness, internal consistency and plausibility, and why a low reported rate isn’t always good news.
